iterations.strategy: Iter 0 spent 46.5ms / 62ms in main_scan, dominated by ~258K random reads of name/name.{off,dat} for the running MIN aggregate. Root cause (Q2): name varlen reads are random-access into name.off (33 MB) and name.dat (60 MB), both far exceeding the 12 MB L3 — every name lookup is a cache miss chain. Fix (Category E, storage extension): built name.name.sortorder = int32[N_name] of row indices in lex-ascending name order (~644 ms one-time build, 16 MB file, reusable by any query needing MIN/MAX/top-K of name.name). The revised plan separates the join into two phases: (1) the join pipeline now writes survivors into a candidate_pid bitset (~520 KB, fits L2) instead of doing per-row name MIN updates; (2) MIN is computed by sequentially scanning sortorder and stopping at the first row whose person_id is in the bitset. With ~258K candidate pids out of 4.17M names, the expected first-hit position is ~16, so the MIN phase collapses from ~30 ms of random varlen access to a handful of sequential reads.
